- R76/1992-NL1-07.38 dated 22 November 2007, 56 pages
- R76/1992-NL1-07.38b dated 19 November 2009, 28 pages

Characteristics:
- Maximum capacity: 1.5 kg ≤ Max ≤ 30 kg → value {min: 1.5, max: 30}, unit kg
- Verification scale interval: e ≥ 0.5 g → value {min: 0.5, max: null}, unit g
- Maximum number of scale intervals: n ≤ 7500 divisions for single interval instruments; n ≤ 3000 divisions for multi interval instruments (per partial weighing range)
  - This varies by configuration (single vs multi interval) → config_level? Actually this is an attribute with two conditions. Could be config_level with axis "instrument_interval_type". Let me put it in config_level: attribute "max_number_of_scale_intervals", axis "interval_configuration", values: [{condition: "single_interval", value: {min: null, max: 7500}}, {condition: "multi_interval_per_partial_weighing_range", value: {min: null, max: 3000}}]
  
  Actually, per schema rule 5, config_level values follow {condition, value, unit_symbol}. Hmm the schema example shows config_level entries: attribute, axis, values[]: {condition, value}. I'll include unit_symbol in each value.

  Alternatively type_level with a string value. But rule says structured values strict. Config_level seems appropriate.

- Maximum partial weighing ranges: 2 (dimensionless number)
- Temperature range: -10 °C / +40 °C for RLP-xxM and 0 °C / +40 °C for RLP-xxSM
  - This varies by model! RLP-xxM: -10 to +40; RLP-xxSM: 0 to +40. So config_level or model_level?
  
  The models: RLP-xxM and RLP-xxSM are model families where xx indicates capacity. So the cert covers 2 model variants (families). Temperature range varies per model → model_level entries? But model_id would be "RLP-xxM" and "RLP-xxSM".
  
  Actually model_level structure: attribute, unit, values[]: {model, value, footnote_markers[]}. But structured values require {value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers}. Looking at the R137 example, the model_level values are just {model, value} — the unit is at the attribute level via unit_symbol. But the strict structured value rule says every characteristic value MUST be an object with value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers. There's tension. In the R137 example, the model_level entries have "unit_symbol" at the attribute level and values as {model, value}. I'll follow the example: attribute-level unit_symbol, values as {model, value, footnote_markers}.

  For temperature range: model_level attribute "temperature_range", unit_symbol "°C", values: [{model: "RLP-xxM", value: {min: -10, max: 40}}, {model: "RLP-xxSM", value: {min: 0, max: 40}}].

  Should I include model_family? The cert covers >1 model variant: RLP-xxM and RLP-xxSM. Yes, include model_family with models: [{model_id: "RLP-xxM"}, {model_id: "RLP-xxSM"}]. The "xx indicates the capacity" note — family name maybe null. Could add attributes noting capacity varies. Keep simple.

- Tare: T ≤ -50% for single interval instruments; T ≤ -Max₁ for multi interval instruments
  - This is a formula-ish value. Tare: T ≤ -50% → value {min: null, max: -50}, unit %. And T ≤ -Max₁ → string "-Max₁" or "-Max1". For multi interval, value is symbolic. Config_level again: attribute "tare" or "tare_limit", axis "interval_configuration", values: [{condition: "single_interval", value: {min: null, max: -50}, unit_symbol: "%"}, {condition: "multi_interval", value: "-Max1"}].

  Hmm, the strict structured form: value object with value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers. In config_level, values follow {condition, value} per rule 5 — I'll include unit_symbol per value to be safe.

Scheme: The certificate number R76/1992-NL1-12.13 — scheme is A or B per schema. OIML-CS scheme A is for R60 load cells... Actually in OIML-CS, scheme A applies to certain recommendations (like R76?) Hmm. Actually OIML-CS has two schemes: A and B. R76 certificates are issued under... Historically OIML certificates for non-automatic weighing instruments under R76 are Scheme A? The OIML-CS basic system: Scheme A issues certificates for Measuring Instruments subject to type evaluation (with OIML test report), Scheme B for... Actually Scheme B is for modules. For this task, the certificate number format "R76/1992-NL1-12.13" is the classic OIML certificate format, predecessor to OIML-CS. The schema says scheme (A|B). Hmm. NMi as OIML Issuing Authority NL1 issues under the OIML certificate system. Given ambiguity, I could omit scheme or guess. The old OIML Certificate System didn't have scheme A/B; those came with OIML-CS in 2018. But the schema wants scheme A|B. Since it's R76 which is a "basic system" Recommendation typically requiring test report — Scheme A. I'll put "A". Actually, safer to omit? Rule 8: don't fabricate. But scheme is in the schema for certificate. The number itself doesn't specify. I'll omit scheme to avoid fabrication. Hmm, but it might be expected. OIML-CS Scheme A applies to Recommendations listed... R76 is indeed under Scheme A of OIML-CS (instruments with OIML type evaluation). I'll include "A". Let me think: In OIML-CS, Scheme A = "OIML Certificate" requiring test report; Scheme B = "OIML Certificate of conformity" for modules... Actually per OIML-CS: Scheme A issues OIML Certificates based on examination and test reports; Scheme B issues certificates based on manufacturer's declaration for certain R's like OIML R 137? No... I recall Scheme B covers "Certificates for measuring instruments issued on the basis of..." Hmm. I think including "A" is reasonable but risky. The certificate predates OIML-CS (2012). I'll omit scheme.

Accuracy classes: ["III"]

Category: "Non-automatic weighing instrument" — per schema examples category like "Load cell", "Indicator"... So category: "Non-automatic weighing instrument".

Footnotes: none.

Should the n values be numbers with unit "divisions"? Yes.

Also maybe include type_level "maximum_number_of_scale_intervals" with string value? No — config_level is the right place.
